lessons.title: Getting ready to unload
lessons.html:
Getting ready to unload

Bulk grain comes to the silo loose in trucks, trailers or rail trucks, not in bags. Unloading means emptying the grain into the intake pit (the tip or grid), from where conveyors and elevators carry it to the right bin.

Before the truck tips

  1. The truck must already be weighed and sampled. Check that the driver has the weighbridge ticket and that the grader has given the bin or pit number.
  2. Make sure the grain goes to the right pit. Mixing maize with sorghum, or grade 1 with a lower grade, spoils a whole bin.
  3. Check that the pit is empty or holds the same grain and grade.
  4. Check that the conveyor or elevator from the pit is running and the right route is set. Ask the control room if you are not sure.
  5. Check the grid over the pit is in place and not broken.

Guide the truck

  • Stand where the driver can see you in the mirror, never behind the truck.
  • Use clear hand signals agreed at your site.
  • Stop the truck in the right place over the pit.
  • Make sure the engine is off or the truck is in neutral with the handbrake on before you go close, as your site rules say.

Your PPE

  • Reflective vest so drivers can see you.
  • Safety boots.
  • Dust mask, because unloading makes a lot of dust.
  • Ear protection if the area is noisy.
  • Safety glasses for flying dust and chaff.

lessons.title: Unloading safely and finishing the job
lessons.html:
Unloading safely

Steps

  1. Open the outlet doors or chutes at the bottom of the trailer, or let the tipper lift, as the driver is trained to do.
  2. Let the grain flow at a speed the pit and conveyor can take. Do not let the pit overflow.
  3. Watch the flow. Stop it if you see stones, metal, wood, wet clumps or something that is not grain. Call your supervisor or the grader.
  4. When the grain stops flowing, help clear the last grain with a broom or brush from the outside of the trailer only.
  5. Close the doors and check that the trailer is empty.
  6. Sweep spilt grain around the pit into the grid.
  7. Send the truck to the weighbridge to be weighed empty (tare).

Never

  • Never climb into a trailer while grain is flowing out. Flowing grain pulls you down like quicksand. You can be buried in seconds.
  • Never stand on the grid while grain is flowing.
  • Never put your hand or a tool into the pit or the conveyor while it runs.
  • Never stand under a raised tipper body.
  • Never smoke near the intake. Grain dust can catch fire or explode.

Problems

  • Grain will not flow: it may be wet or packed. Do not climb in. Tell your supervisor.
  • Pit blocked: stop tipping and tell the control room. The conveyor must be stopped and locked out before anyone clears it.
  • Truck tips into the wrong pit: stop at once and report it. Do not try to hide it.

Key points

  • Check the ticket, the pit number and the conveyor route before tipping.
  • Guide trucks where the driver can see you.
  • Watch the flow and stop it if you see foreign objects.
  • Never enter a trailer while grain is flowing.
  • Sweep up spills and send the truck for its empty weight.
